---
title: "Fit a Stan model with MCMC"
---

Fit the eight schools hierarchical model with four MCMC chains, then print a posterior summary, the sampler's warnings, and draws of `tau`.

Compiling a model needs CmdStan and a C++ toolchain, as described in [Installation](../installation.qmd). The data are the estimated coaching effects `y` and their standard errors `sigma` for eight schools (Rubin 1981), also available as [schools.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/schools.csv).

```php
use function CmdStan\cmdstan_model;
use function CmdStan\write_stan_file;

$code = <<<'STAN'
data {
  int<lower=1> J;
  vector[J] y;
  vector<lower=0>[J] sigma;
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> tau;
  vector[J] theta_raw;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[J] theta = mu + tau * theta_raw;
}
model {
  mu ~ normal(0, 10);
  tau ~ normal(0, 10);
  theta_raw ~ std_normal();
  y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
}
STAN;

$file = write_stan_file(
    $code,
    dir: __DIR__,
    basename: 'schools',
);
$model = cmdstan_model($file);

$data = [
    'J' => 8,
    'y' => [28, 8, -3, 7, -1, 1, 18, 12],
    'sigma' => [15, 10, 16, 11, 9, 11, 10, 18],
];

$fit = $model->sample(
    data: $data,
    seed: 123,
    chains: 4,
    parallel_chains: 4,
    adapt_delta: 0.95,
    show_messages: false,
);

$rows = $fit->summary(['mu', 'tau', 'theta']);
echo "variable   mean    sd     q5    q95  rhat ess_bulk\n";
foreach ($rows as $r) {
    printf(
        "%-8s %6.2f %5.2f %6.2f %6.2f %5.3f %8.0f\n",
        $r['variable'],
        $r['mean'],
        $r['sd'],
        $r['q5'],
        $r['q95'],
        $r['rhat'],
        $r['ess_bulk'],
    );
}

$warnings = $fit->diagnosticWarnings();
echo $warnings ? implode("\n", $warnings) : 'No warnings';
echo "\n";

$draws = $fit->draws('tau', 'draws_matrix');
$tau = array_column($draws, 'tau');
echo count($tau), " draws of tau, the first five:\n";
$first = array_slice($tau, 0, 5);
printf("%.2f, %.2f, %.2f, %.2f, %.2f\n", ...$first);
```

Output:

```text
variable   mean    sd     q5    q95  rhat ess_bulk
mu         6.40  4.06  -0.31  13.12 1.001     3582
tau        4.78  3.75   0.37  12.00 1.000     2176
theta[1]   8.87  6.90  -0.84  21.11 1.000     4184
theta[2]   6.72  5.47  -2.11  15.66 1.001     5706
theta[3]   5.37  6.35  -5.21  14.78 1.001     4311
theta[4]   6.64  5.63  -2.76  15.59 1.001     4613
theta[5]   4.83  5.50  -4.85  13.22 1.001     4452
theta[6]   5.46  5.79  -4.55  14.29 1.000     4957
theta[7]   8.75  5.91   0.12  19.22 1.002     4966
theta[8]   6.90  6.39  -3.13  17.47 1.001     4643
No warnings
4000 draws of tau, the first five:
1.41, 1.36, 1.63, 0.63, 0.06
```

- `write_stan_file()` rewrites `schools.stan` only when the program changes, so the model compiles on the first run and later runs reuse the executable.
- Four chains of 1,000 sampling iterations, after 1,000 warmup iterations, give 4,000 draws per variable.
- Partial pooling pulls each school's `theta` toward `mu`. The pull is stronger when `tau` is small or a school's `sigma` is large.
- The non-centered form, `theta = mu + tau * theta_raw`, usually produces far fewer divergent transitions than sampling `theta` directly. It does not rule them out.
- Use the estimates only when `rhat` is below 1.01, `ess_bulk` is at least 100 per chain, and there are no warnings.
- A fixed seed reproduces the draws only with the same CmdStan version, compiler, and machine.
